findings.title: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when `embed_category` (or `uncategorized_category_id`) has no row in site_settings
findings.body: `execute("SELECT ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` indexes into a PG::Result. Sites that never changed `embed_category` have no row in `site_settings`, because defaults are not stored. Fresh installs and most upgraded sites are in this case. `[0]` is then nil and `nil['id']` raises, so the whole migration aborts and `embeddable_hosts` is never created. The fallback on line 15 has the same problem: `execute("SELECT value ... 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value']` fails if that row is missing. Use `.first`/`.ntuples` checks and fall back to a default instead of assuming a row exists.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are inserted raw: not normalized, not SQL-escaped, blanks not skipped
findings.body: The old `embeddable_hosts` setting allowed entries like `http://eviltrout.com` and values with surrounding whitespace or blank lines. The migration inserts each line verbatim with string interpolation, so it bypasses the model's `before_validation` that strips the scheme and path. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` with `URI(...).host`, so a row stored as `http://eviltrout.com` can never match. Every site that used the documented scheme-prefixed format silently loses embedding after upgrade. Blank lines become empty-host rows, and a quote in a value breaks the SQL statement. Strip the scheme and path, strip whitespace, skip blanks, and quote with `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote`.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped between category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb
findings.body: `category_fabricator.rb` now holds only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`. The `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators were moved into `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. Fabrication loads every file in the directory, so tests still run. But the file names no longer match their contents, so anyone looking for the category fabricators will not find them. It also looks like a copy/rename mistake that will cause confusion or merge conflicts later. Each file should contain its own fabricators.

findings.title: update/destroy dereference nil when the host id doesn't exist
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown or already-deleted id. `save_host(nil)` then calls `host.host=` on nil, and `destroy` calls `host.destroy` on nil. Both raise NoMethodError, so the client gets a 500 instead of a 404. Double-clicking delete or editing a stale list would trigger this. Use `find_by` plus an explicit not-found response, or `find`, so `RecordNotFound` is handled.

findings.title: Missing params cause 500s; nil host blows up in the model's before_validation
findings.body: `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` raises if the `embeddable_host` key is absent. If `host` is absent or nil, `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!` on nil and raises NoMethodError. Both cases give a 500 instead of a validation error from `render_json_error`. The model callback should guard against nil, and the controller should use `params.require(:embeddable_host)`. The category id is also never checked to exist.

findings.title: Host lookup ignores case of the input and can never match hosts stored with a port
findings.body: The query is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, where `host` is `uri.host` taken straight from the referer or embed URL. Only the column is lowercased, so a referer such as `http://Example.COM/...` never matches a stored `example.com`. The validation regex explicitly allows a `:port` suffix, and `before_validation` only strips from the first `/`, so `example.com:8080` is stored with its port. `uri.host` never includes a port, so such a record can never match any request. Normalize with `host.downcase` and decide consistently whether ports are stored or compared.

findings.title: Host validation is overly restrictive and there is no uniqueness check
findings.body: The regex requires a final label of 2-5 letters. This rejects `localhost`, intranet names, IPs and longer TLDs such as `.photography` or `.technology`. The old free-text setting accepted these, so admins can no longer add or re-save them. There is also no uniqueness validation on `host`, so the same host can be added repeatedly, each with a possibly different category. Which category an imported topic gets is then arbitrary, because `.first` has no ordering.

findings.title: expandable_first_post? specs have a misleading name and a no-op fixture
findings.body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer looks at embeddable hosts. The test "is false if embeddable_host is blank" actually passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and there is no topic embed, so it does not test what its name says. In the `'with an emeddable host'` context (typo included) the `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` has no effect on the result. The specs should be renamed or cleaned up to reflect the new behavior.

findings.title: New admin endpoints have no behavioral tests
findings.body: The new `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` and `Admin::EmbeddingController` are covered only by a test that they subclass AdminController. There are no tests for create/update/destroy, validation errors, a missing id, default-category fallback, or non-staff access. The 500 paths in the controller therefore go unnoticed. The migration is also untested.

findings.title: Client assigns a category that may differ from what the server saved
findings.body: When no category is chosen, the server falls back to the uncategorized category id. After saving, the component sets `host.category` to `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))`, which is undefined for a blank id. The row then shows an empty category badge until the page is reloaded, even though the server stored Uncategorized. Use the `category_id` from the server response instead of the local `categoryId`.
